title: SLA-aware heterogeneous mini-canary with adaptive shadow fallback and automated rollback advisor
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: New mini-canary controller: SLA-aware routing decisions, heterogeneous capacity support, adaptive shadow fallback and automated rollback advisor. Backwards compatible with existing rollout API. Recommended default config provided.
description:
Context & motivation: Many customers must run canaries across heterogeneous pools (mixed GPU types, dedicated vs shared) while respecting tenant-level SLAs. Existing staged-canary machinery assumes homogeneous capacity and a single SLO target; this led to manual intervention when one pool saturated, and caused customer-visible latency regressions during a recent dedicated-capacity incident. This PR implements a compact 'mini-canary' controller that is SLA-aware, can route a small progressive fraction across heterogeneous backends, and fall back to shadow routing when live capacity cannot meet SLA commitments.

Design summary: Adds a lightweight controller (Minicanary) that: 1) periodically samples per-pool latency and error distributions, 2) computes projected SLO adherence for proposed traffic fractions, 3) applies conservative routing when heterogeneity or overload is detected, and 4) triggers an automated rollback advisor if cumulative SLO risk exceeds configured thresholds. The controller uses existing metrics (p99 latency, 5xx rate, token-per-request cost) and integrates with the runtime's smart routing policy. It runs as an opt-in sub-controller for rollouts and defaults to safe, small fractions (0.5% start).

Implementation notes: - pkg/rollout/minicanary/controller.go: core FSM, sampling window, budget accounting and decision engine. - pkg/rollout/minicanary/slo_estimator.go: statistical projection model (bootstrap-based distribution projection) and toleration calculus. - pkg/rollout/minicanary/shadow_bridge.go: lightweight shadow mirroring path that preserves headers and deterministic sampling for replay. - pkg/rollout/advisor/rollback_advisor.go: interprets telemetry and suggests immediate rollback, conditional pause, or gradual backoff. - configs/defaults/minicanary.yaml: safe defaults and per-tenant knobs (initial_fraction, max_fraction, slo_risk_threshold, pool_priorities). - cmd/cli/rolloutctl/observe.go: new subcommand 'rolloutctl minicanary simulate' for dry-run projections.

Compatibility & migration: The Minicanary controller is registerable via the rollout CRD's 'strategy' field. Default behavior requires explicit opt-in by adding strategy: minicanary. No breaking changes to existing staged canary or shadow flows; existing controllers continue to function. Backwards compatible with release/main.

Testing & validation: Unit tests: controller FSM transitions, slo estimator statistical properties, and advisor decision thresholds. Integration: local canary e2e that simulates heterogeneous pools (A100, T4, CPU) with synthetic latency skews. Staging: ran a 72-hour canary sweep on the staging fleet exercising saturation and autoscale; runtime routing correctly demoted live traffic to shadow and emitted advisor alerts. Load test: replayed PriorIncident-2026-01-12 trace; minicanary prevented a 3x p99 spike by shifting 70% of canary traffic to shadow when pool throttling detected. CI: final CI run passed all gates.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CLI dry-run tool - [x] Default config - [x] Docs: runbook and playbook draft - [x] Release notes

Docs & runbook: Added docs/runbooks/minicanary-playbook.md with step-by-step operator guidance, signals to watch, common mitigations, and how to pin to dedicated pools. Also extended docs/rollouts/strategies.md with configuration examples.

Security & cost: No secret changes. Shadow mirroring is samplable and off by default; mirrors are rate-limited to avoid doubling cost in steady-state. Advisor emits decision traces to centralized audit log for post-incident analysis.

Follow-ups: - ENG-3603: autoscale-integration to allow minicanary to request temporary burst capacity for short-lived canaries. - ENG-3627: expand advisor heuristics to include semantic-quality regressions (prompt-based smoke tests).

review_comments: Marco Hernández: Can we avoid turning on shadow mirroring by default? Please ensure sampling is off unless explicitly enabled in tenant config.
Aisha Patel: Agreed; shadow defaults to disabled and sampling_rate must be set by tenant. Updated configs/defaults/minicanary.yaml to reflect this.
Leah Kim: SLO estimator looks solid; add a comment describing the bootstrap assumptions and where to tune confidence level.
Aisha Patel: Added detailed doc comments and exposed confidence_level knob in config (default 95%).
Dmitri Volkov: Suggest adding a metric for 'advisor_suggested_rollback' and a circuit-breaker telemetry tag so SRE can build alerts.
Aisha Patel: Added advisor_suggested_rollback counter and circuit_breaker.tier tag to telemetry_bindings.go
Leah Kim: Integration tests flaky on first run due to timing window; recommended increasing sampling window for CI environment.
Aisha Patel: Increased CI sampling window and added a deterministic seed for the synthetic latency generator. CI re-run passed.
merge: Merged via squash and merge by Marco Hernández on 2026-02-25. Commit message condensed features and credits reviewers.
post_merge_notes: Feature gated by rollout.strategy=minicanary. Ops should enable on a single customer namespace first. Watch advisor_suggested_rollback and p99_delta metrics during rollout. See runbook for rollback playbook.
notes_for_release: Ship as experimental feature in 0.41.0, disabled-by-default. Admins may opt-in per-tenant. Follow-up tasks scheduled (ENG-3603, ENG-3627).
